author: GamingBolt
description:
Halloween: The Game tries to bring Michael Myers to life in our hands, but has it managed the switch from the movies to a video game well enough for the effort to succeed? 

That’s precisely what we’re here to answer in our review. We played the story and dabbled in the game’s multiplayer offerings long enough to know this is a good effort, but it might not necessarily draw you in whether you’re a fan of its slasher-film inspirations or not. We’re diving deep into this one, and you’re going to want to see this if you’ve been thinking of trying your hand at being one of popular culture’s most terrifying presences.
title: Halloween: The Game Review - The Final Verdict

author: GamingBolt
description:
Perhaps Onimusha Way of the Sword got a little too carried away at finally reviving Onimusha that the game wanted to stuff as much as possible into the experience. The result isn't a terrible game by any means, and if nothing else, the fact that the gameplay beyond the combat is satisfying should show that it's worth the price of admission. It just would've been nice to zero in on that more, especially when the other aspects feel noticeably weaker by comparison.

A lesson for the future perhaps, because I find it hard to believe that the the developer would go to such lengths to effectively soft reboot the franchise. For now, Onimusha: Way of the Sword will satisfy you if it's swordplay, incredible production values, and stellar boss fights that you're after. Just try not to let the fluff dull those moments.
title: Onimusha: Way of the Sword's Combat Is SO GOOD It Hides Some Surprising Problems

author: GamingBolt
description:
Taking inspiration from real-world locations as much as Silent Hill’s earlier entries, Silent Hill: Townfall is the latest stab at the storied survival horror series, and it’s another experience set outside the USA following last year’s Silent Hill f. 

With mysteries to unravel, monsters to evade, and a game-defining handheld TV to guide you, Townfall is poised to be more than simply ‘Silent Hill in Scotland’. From real-world fog, to combat strategies and difficulty settings, here’s fifteen things you need to know before you buy Silent Hill: Townfall.
title: Silent Hill: Townfall - 15 Things You Need To Know Before You Buy
